**Problem:**

A point is chosen at random on a line segment 10 cm long. Two marks are placed on the segment: one at the 3 cm mark and one at the 7 cm mark. What is the probability that the random point is closer to the 3 cm mark than to the 7 cm mark?

**Solution:**

The point is closer to the 3 cm mark when its distance to 3 is less than its distance to 7.

|x − 3| < |x − 7|

This simplifies to x < 5 (the midpoint between 3 and 7).

So the favorable region is 0 ≤ x < 5, which has length 5.

Probability = 5/10 = **0.5**

**Problem:** A point is chosen at random on a line segment of length 10. Two spots are marked at positions 3 and 7 from the left end. What is the probability that the randomly chosen point is closer to the spot at position 3 than to the spot at position 7?

**Solution:**

The midpoint between position 3 and position 7 is **(3 + 7) / 2 = 5**.

A point on the segment is closer to position 3 than to position 7 if and only if it lies to the **left** of position 5 (i.e., in the interval [0, 5]).

The favorable length is **5** (from 0 to 5), and the total segment length is **10**.

**Probability = 5 / 10 = 0.5**
